name: ema_crossover_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: EMA(9) crossing above EMA(21) on 1-min bars signals a short-term momentum shift. The 9-bar EMA captures the last ~9 minutes of sentiment while the 21-bar EMA captures the last ~21 minutes. A cross indicates that short-term buying pressure has overtaken medium-term average price, often signaling the start of an intraday trend leg. The edge exists because EMA crossovers, while simple, work better in Indian markets due to higher trending behavior (longer institutional order execution times vs US markets, leading to extended intraday trends). The key filter is ADX(14) > 25 to confirm a trending environment — crossovers in rangebound markets are chopped up. The edge is thin and depends on capturing 2-3 good trend legs per day while keeping losses small on false crossovers.

long.confirmation: cross bar closes in top 40% of its range AND volume > 1.2x SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: cross bar closes in bottom 40% of its range AND volume > 1.2x SMA(volume, 10)

entry.entry_price: market order on cross bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry OR EMA(9) re-crosses EMA(21) in opposite direction

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — momentum works across VIX regimes
other_filters: skip if EMA(9) and EMA(21) have crossed >4 times in last 60 bars (choppy market)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — EMA crossover is the most basic TA signal; edge depends on ADX filter and execution speed

weaknesses: Win rate is low (~42%) — requires psychological discipline to endure losing streaks of 5-8 trades
EMA crossover on 1-min bars generates many false signals even with ADX filter — choppy days accumulate losses
The signal is extremely well-known and taught in every beginner trading course — crowding risk is high
prior_art: EMA crossover is perhaps the most widely known trading signal (Murphy, 'Technical Analysis'). ADX as a trend strength filter is from Wilder (1978). The 9/21 EMA pair is commonly used by retail traders globally. Adding ADX and VWAP filters provides some differentiation but the core signal is generic.
notes: Edge math: 0.42 * 40bps - 0.58 * 20bps = 16.8 - 11.6 = 5.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -5.8 bps. Negative. EMA crossover alone is not sufficient for profitability after costs on 1-min bars. The ADX filter and VWAP alignment are essential but still insufficient. Strategy is best used as a directional bias signal combined with better entry timing (e.g., EMA cross for direction, then VWAP reversion for entry).
